claim: The Unbound licence price ($28/fund-yr base) is computed at a whole-platform scale of 1,000,000 funds (favourable 3,000,000), which exceeds the entire US traditional invested DAF market (<=737k accounts) and requires ~200 sponsors of 5,000 funds when only 20 US sponsors of any kind hold >=5,000 accounts. At the platform's own cost floor, Unbound loses ~$4.2M/yr at 100k funds and breaks even (before sales, implementation, capex and margin) only near ~490k funds / ~100 sponsors.
evidence: /home/user/daf-landscape/research/DAF-INDUSTRY-REPORT-2026-11.md:27-28 (3.59m reported accounts, 79.5% in donation processors; traditional invested accounts <=737k)

/home/user/daf-landscape/data/mission-2026-11-14/dafrc-sponsor-schedule-d-fy2019-2024.csv FY2024 recomputation: 20 sponsors >=5,000 accounts holding 3.39M accounts, of which Givinga/AOGF/PayPal processors ~2.84M
scratchpad work/exp*.py (re-runs of enterprise_economics.py with overrides; repository unchanged): OM3 vendor cost $6.97M vs licence revenue $2.78M at 100k funds; break-even ~490k-500k funds
why_it_matters: Every C/D cost advantage, E4/E5 viability and the 'licence is small' conclusion depend on a market share Unbound cannot reach; at realistic early scale (25k-250k funds) the licence is $49-$229/fund, not $28.
recommended_change: Replace the licence scale assumption with an adoption-ramp scenario grounded in the sponsor-size distribution (DAFRC FY2024): the licence price used in any comparison SHALL be computed at the platform scale reachable in years 1-5 by named target sponsors; acceptance: model reports C and D results at 25k, 50k, 100k and 250k platform funds and the 1M/3M cases are labelled 'exceeds addressable market'.

claim: There is no model of Unbound's own P&L. The licence floor explicitly excludes Unbound's sales, marketing, implementation and customer acquisition (selling to sponsors), and build capex ($5M, range $3-15M) is not recovered in the licence. Vendor engineering is capped at 10 FTE and security at 3 for a SOC 1/SOC 2, multi-tenant, bank/custodian/ERP-integrated platform with 1,176 requirements and 63 convergence clauses. The only margin is a 30% markup (~$6.4M/yr even at the unreachable 1M funds).
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/discovery/2026-11-24-simplification-economics/model/decision_teams.py:221 ('Floors recover modelled vendor cost only; margin, sales and customer acquisition excluded')
why_it_matters: The business case presented is the customers' business case (sponsor margins of $582-$1,460/fund), not Unbound's; an investor cannot evaluate payback, burn or capital need from these artifacts.
recommended_change: Add a vendor P&L requirement to the economic model: revenue ramp by named segment, Unbound sales/implementation/customer-success cost per sponsor won, build and maintenance capex, compliance staff, SOC audit fees, and cash breakeven; acceptance: model outputs cumulative cash need, payback year and breakeven sponsors under base and adverse adoption.

claim: The initial market hypothesis (community foundation / independent sponsor entry, SPD-CMP-001) is contradicted by the repository's own data. E2 is modelled at 1,500 funds (range 500-5,000), but the median US community foundation has 46 DAFs, p90 313, only 7 of 803 have >=1,500 and none has 5,000; all 803 CFs together hold ~104k DAF accounts. Re-running E2 at 150 and 300 funds, approach C costs MORE than traditional workflows on licensed software (AL): $5,664 vs $5,390 at 150 funds, $2,915 vs $2,775 at 300.
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/model/enterprise_economics.py:60-63 (E2 accounts 1500, scales 500/1500/5000, basis '[A] hundreds to low thousands')
/home/user/daf-landscape/data/mission-2026-11-14/dafrc-sponsor-schedule-d-fy2019-2024.csv FY2024 CF rows: n=803, accounts 104,425, median 46, p75 128, p90 313, >=1500: 7
scratchpad work/exp*.py (re-runs of enterprise_economics.py with overrides; repository unchanged): E2 AL vs C at 50/150/300/1500 funds
why_it_matters: The beachhead segment is too small to fund the platform (100% of CF DAFs at $28 = ~$2.9M ARR) and, for the typical CF, the AI-native redesign produces no saving over incumbent-style software; the CF 'win' (EV-02) is a build-vs-buy artifact against a self-built baseline no CF uses.
recommended_change: Decide SPD-CMP-001 only after re-running E2 at the observed CF size distribution (median 46, p90 313 DAFs) and against AL priced at incumbent licence levels; acceptance: a CF entry is approved only if C beats AL at the p50 and p75 CF size and Unbound's per-tenant revenue covers the $52k tenant cost floor.

claim: Community foundations need one system for all fund types (DAF, field-of-interest, designated, scholarship, endowment, competitive grantmaking); E2 explicitly excludes non-DAF programmes from scope. Foundant CommunitySuite runs 361 of 803 CFs (45%, 32.7% of mapped CF DAF assets) and every dated CF portal switch in the census landed on Foundant. A DAF-only product forces a CF to run two systems.
evidence: /home/user/daf-landscape/research/DAF-INDUSTRY-REPORT-2026-11.md:436-457 (CF vendor map; all six dated CF portal switches end on Foundant)
why_it_matters: Foundant's breadth of fund types, installed base and migration momentum is a durable advantage no convergence clause answers; CF entry without non-DAF fund types is not a credible offer.
recommended_change: Either (a) add a requirement scoping non-DAF CF fund types (designated, field-of-interest, scholarship, agency, endowment spending) with acceptance tests, or (b) record as accepted limitation that CFs are not a release-1 segment; acceptance: SPD-CMP-001 record cites the chosen option.

claim: The headline A-vs-C saving is largely an assumption artefact. Approach A is forced to a 30% exception rate (the 'broad proxy') while B, C and D use the 8% 'core proxy'; neither is observed review. Re-running A at 8% drops E1 A from $465 to $320 and E4 from $87 to $62: ~46% of the E1 A->C gap (145 of 316) comes from that single assumption, not from redesign.
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:30 ('2.8% per-grant [S]; 7-8.5% core proxy [S]; broad proxy likely 28-31%; none is observed review')
scratchpad work/exp*.py (re-runs of enterprise_economics.py with overrides; repository unchanged): A with exception_rate 0.08 -> E1 320, E2 3215, E3 634, E4 62, E5 231
why_it_matters: Executives quoting '68% cheaper than traditional' would be quoting a definitional mismatch; the honest comparator is B or AL at the same exception definition.
recommended_change: Require all approaches in a comparison to use the same exception definition and source; differences in exception incidence between approaches SHALL be stated as separate named levers with their own evidence; acceptance: model run log lists every per-approach override with its evidence label and a 'same-definition' A is reported alongside.

claim: The C advantage over AI-enhanced incumbents (B) rests on unmeasured C-only levers, chiefly complex-asset handling cut from 12 to 2 hours (with a $350 fund-borne vendor fee) and 50% determination reuse. Removing the complex-hours lever alone adds $61/fund to E1 and $244 to E3; removing all C levers leaves E1 C at $255 vs B $313, and at a realistic licence (platform 100k funds, $91) C is no cheaper than B. Outsourcing complex assets is equally available to incumbents.
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/model/enterprise_economics.py:78-80 (LEVERS_C: determination_reuse 0.5, minutes x0.667, contacts x0.6, recon x0.3, complex_hours set 2.0)

scratchpad work/exp*.py (re-runs of enterprise_economics.py with overrides; repository unchanged) exp2.py lever-removal deltas: E1 complex_hours +61.4, determination_reuse +17.7; E3 complex_hours +243.7
why_it_matters: The cost case flips against an incumbent that adopts exception-based review and outsources complex gifts, which EV-03 already concedes; the durable residue is small and unmeasured.
recommended_change: Add complex-gift handling hours and determination-reuse share to the CNV-EVB-001 measurement list with a 90-day time study at a real sponsor; until measured, headline comparisons SHALL show C with B-equivalent levers (no reuse, minutes x1.0, complex 12h) as the base case and the levers as upside.

claim: Headline figures are deterministic 'expected values' that sit below the model's own favourable P10 (E1 C $149 vs P10 $170, P50 $209, P90 $253; E3 C $289 vs P10 $339), and report 05 headlines the deterministic number.
why_it_matters: Decision-makers will anchor on a number better than the model's own optimistic tail; P50 is 40% higher for E1.
recommended_change: Require economic headlines to use Monte Carlo P50 with P10-P90 range; deterministic values only as a labelled reference; acceptance: render_tables output headline column = P50.

claim: Licence per-tenant cost is amortised over 5,000 funds for every enterprise (tenant floor $52k/yr / 5000), so small tenants are under-charged: a 1,500-fund CF should bear ~$35/fund of tenant cost, a 150-fund CF ~$347/fund. At base licence a 150-fund CF pays Unbound ~$4.2k/yr against a $52k vendor tenant cost.
evidence: scratchpad work/exp*.py (re-runs of enterprise_economics.py with overrides; repository unchanged) exp4.py
why_it_matters: Unbound loses money on every small sponsor at the modelled price, precisely the proposed entry segment.
recommended_change: Correct the model to charge the tenant fee on each enterprise's actual funds per sponsor, and add a pricing rule: tenant fee SHALL recover at least the per-tenant cost floor for each sponsor-size band; acceptance: no sponsor-size band shows negative vendor contribution in the base case.

claim: Under adverse but plausible people costs the administrator model (E5) loses money: E5 margin is $46/fund at $200 institutional licensing; at loaded cost $250k/FTE it is -$4 (base licence) and -$25 (adverse licence); at 17% exceptions x 90 min with adverse licence, +$4.
evidence: scratchpad work/exp*.py (re-runs of enterprise_economics.py with overrides; repository unchanged) exp4.py E5 rows
why_it_matters: E5 is cited as a viable route for many sponsors, but its margin is thinner than the uncertainty in any single people-cost input.
recommended_change: Add an acceptance criterion: an enterprise configuration SHALL be described as viable only if contribution margin is positive at P90 cost and adverse licence; E5 to be relabelled 'not demonstrated' until measured.

claim: E3 (advisor-distributed, the highest modelled margin at $1,460/fund) assumes advisor-managed funds paying tiered advisor fees with a 50% platform share, but the evidence dossier adopted into the baseline states 'Release 1 has no advisor-managed DAF program' and blocks compensation from a fund to a donor-designated advisor (automatic §4958 excess benefit). The modelled revenue for E3 is therefore not available at release 1.
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/02-EVIDENCE-DOSSIERS.md:330-372 (RCD-021 dossier: business assumption 'Release 1 has no advisor-managed DAF program'; DONOR_ADVISOR_COMPENSATION block)
why_it_matters: The most attractive enterprise in report 05 contradicts the adopted requirements; advisors, the main distribution channel for HNW DAFs, get no compensation path.
recommended_change: Either remove E3 from release-1 economics or add a requirement defining the sponsor-engaged-manager programme (uniform sponsor contract, no donor designation) with acceptance tests, and re-run E3 revenue under that structure.

claim: No distribution partner has an economic reason to push Unbound-based sponsors: referral compensation is disabled, Unbound may take no asset-, trade- or liquidation-linked compensation, donor-designated advisors cannot be paid from funds, and embedded checkout is rated 'easy to copy'. Incumbents (Ren/RCF across ~11 wealth-firm programmes; Fidelity/Schwab/Vanguard affiliates) align distribution with asset economics.
evidence: CNV-LEG-001 statement (no compensation varying with assets)
why_it_matters: The model's $400 CAC assumes an advisor channel that the requirements remove incentives for; without channel incentives CAC is likely higher and volume lower.
recommended_change: Add a business-policy record defining lawful partner incentives (fixed-fee platform partnerships, registered referral where permitted) and an evidence task to obtain partner willingness-to-distribute from at least three wealth platforms before E1/E3 volumes are used.

claim: Customer acquisition is a single assumed $400 per donor account ('no public DAF CAC') applied identically to every enterprise, and sponsor acquisition by Unbound (enterprise sales to 501(c)(3) boards, 6-12 month cycles) is unmodelled. AEF's platform change took ~9 months (Jul 2025 selection to Apr 2026 cut-over).
evidence: /home/user/daf-landscape/research/revenue-retention-and-switching-2026-11-11.md:10,50 (AEF July 2025 -> April 2026; two years of history in new portal)
why_it_matters: Sponsor-level margins survive higher donor CAC (E1 still ~$237/fund at CAC $1,000 and an entrant mix) but Unbound's ramp, cash need and the number of sponsors per year are driven by sponsor CAC and sales cycle, which are absent.
recommended_change: Add an evidence task to obtain sponsor sales-cycle length and implementation cost from at least three recent platform migrations (AEF/Ren, Foundant CF conversions); add sponsor CAC and time-to-live as model parameters with ranges.

claim: E1 revenue is concentrated: 46% of the $693/fund blended revenue comes from 4.5% of accounts (HNW 4% at $1.5M and institutional 0.5% at $10M). A new independent sponsor without institutional accounts and half the HNW share earns ~$498/fund (-28%), and under a Daffy-style subscription the market mix yields ~$86/fund, below C's $149 cost.
evidence: scratchpad work/exp*.py (re-runs of enterprise_economics.py with overrides; repository unchanged) exp3.py
why_it_matters: Loss of a few large funds (death, transfer to a family foundation, advisor move) moves sponsor economics more than any operational lever; fee compression toward flat subscriptions flips E1 to loss.
recommended_change: Add revenue-concentration and fee-compression scenarios to the model (top-5% account loss; subscription and flat-fee pricing); acceptance: E1 viability reported under 'entrant mix' and 'subscription' revenue cases.

claim: Report 05 rates 'shared verified charity knowledge' and 'deterministic controls with integrated evidence' as Hard to copy, contradicting the earlier executive finding that almost no advantage is inherent and competitors are superior in distribution, scale, APIs and charity payment networks. No new evidence supports the upgrade. Fidelity has 204,614 accounts, FMR-provided systems (990 shows $0 IT), an all-in floor of ~50-52 bps and 67% of grants already by EFT.
evidence: /home/user/daf-landscape/research/DAF-INDUSTRY-REPORT-2026-11.md:450-451 (Fidelity: FMR provides record-keeping, $0 IT, no employees)
why_it_matters: Overstated moats lead to under-investment in the actual moats (distribution, assured operating record, executed migrations); the charity-facts registry uses public data and incumbents already hold larger grant histories.
recommended_change: Correct report 05 section 4 to align with SPF-CMP-001: rate each advantage with evidence; 'Hard' only where a measured asset exists (e.g. count of verified determinations, assured SOC period); acceptance: every durability rating cites evidence or is labelled hypothesis.

claim: Ren serves ~30 sponsors holding $48.5bn and can offer a sponsoring charity (RCF), staffed administration and grant vetting. SPD-ADV-004 makes Unbound software-only and SPD-ADV-001 forbids shared decision teams, so a small sponsor that wants to outsource work must hire 2.5 FTE (~$412k/yr) or keep its incumbent. Incumbent per-account take is far higher (RCF->Ren $744 per year-end DAF FY2024) because it bundles services.
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/discovery/2026-11-24-simplification-economics/model/parameters.json:1805 (institutional_licensing source: RCF->Ren $744.48 per year-end DAF FY2024, not ARPU)
why_it_matters: For most sponsors below ~10,700 funds the buying decision is about who does the work, not software cost; a software-only offer loses to bundled service providers.
recommended_change: Record as a business-policy decision with an explicit trigger: re-open SPR-ADV-009 (Unbound-supplied or partner-supplied staffed service via a certified administrator network) if fewer than N sponsors below 10k funds sign within 12 months; add administrator-partner certification requirements.

claim: The routine-grant automation that drives the economics requires, per sponsor: a board resolution delegating approval (CNV-GRT-001), auditor acceptance of the SoD design and deterministic release (CNV-GOV-003), the auditor's written planned approach (CNV-GOV-001), board appointment resolutions (CNV-GOV-004), a controller-approved function map (CNV-FIN-012), CFO fee approval (CNV-ECO-002), an ODFI agreement naming Unbound as TPSP (CNV-PAY-001) and verified custodian feeds (CNV-FIN-013). Until then the three-person rule and individual batch decisions apply. The model assumes these gates are passed from day one.
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/data/convergence-clauses.jsonl (activation_gate fields of CNV-GRT-001, CNV-GOV-001, CNV-GOV-003, CNV-GOV-004, CNV-FIN-012, CNV-FIN-013, CNV-PAY-001, CNV-ECO-002)
/home/user/unbound/requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/05-ECONOMIC-VALIDATION.md:109-113 (failure conditions include auditors refusing reliance and sponsors unable to delegate)
why_it_matters: Time-to-value per sponsor is gated by up to eight external authorizations; first-year economics for each new sponsor are approach AL/B, not C, and boards bear the reputational risk of delegating to an algorithm.
recommended_change: Add a sponsor-activation timeline requirement: the model SHALL compute each sponsor's economics in a pre-delegation phase (no deterministic approval, three-person rule) for a parameterised duration (default 12 months) before C levers apply; acceptance: report includes year-1 per-sponsor cost under pre-delegation operation.

claim: Board-delegated deterministic approval approves conforming grants with no human review. Nothing requires periodic evidence that the sponsor actually exercises variance power and exclusive legal control (e.g. sampled reviews, declines, overrides by humans) or reporting to the board of approval statistics. A regulator or state AG reviewing a sponsor that auto-approves ~92%+ of donor recommendations will ask for proof the control is real.
why_it_matters: Sponsors' §4966/§170 position and AG fiduciary oversight depend on demonstrable control; CNV-GRT-011 sampling measures error, not the exercise of discretion.
recommended_change: Add an acceptance criterion to CNV-GRT-001: the platform SHALL produce a quarterly board report of auto-approved, held, declined and human-reviewed grants with sampled human reviews, and SHALL refuse to renew a delegation whose board has not recorded receipt of the last report.

claim: CNV-LEG-002 treats Unbound's California exposure as a single registration with a moderate-confidence carve-out for sponsor-direct deployments, but white-label is the core product (Type E covers SaaS/white-label platforms) and no work covers other states' charitable solicitation, commercial co-venturer or platform laws, the associated annual reporting, or the cost of compliance staff. Regulatory cost is a fixed $200k legal_base on the customer side only.
evidence: /home/user/daf-landscape/research/DAF-INDUSTRY-REPORT-2026-11.md:722 (Batch 30: white-label portal is Type E; DAF exclusion names only the sponsor)
why_it_matters: A multi-state platform registration burden falls on Unbound itself, not on sponsors, and is absent from the vendor cost; a wrong carve-out would block California, the largest DAF donor state.
recommended_change: Add an evidence task for a 50-state survey of platform/fundraising-counsel/commercial co-venturer registration applicable to a white-label DAF platform, with counsel sign-off, and add the resulting registration and reporting cost as a vendor cost line.

claim: The economics ignore policy risk to the market itself: the 2023 proposed §4966 regulations remain open (personal investment advisor rule, broad DAF definition affecting CF fund classification) with a 2026-27 Priority Guidance Plan item, and OBBBA (effective 2026) adds a 0.5%-of-AGI floor and a 35% value cap for itemizers while the new non-itemizer deduction excludes DAF gifts.
evidence: /home/user/daf-landscape/research/DAF-INDUSTRY-REPORT-2026-11.md:205,767 (proposed regs neither final nor withdrawn; PGP item)
why_it_matters: Final regulations could reclassify CF funds and advisor arrangements (hitting E2 and E3), and the tax changes shift small-balance demand; neither appears as a stress scenario.
recommended_change: Add a 'final §4966 regulations as proposed' and a 'contribution demand -15%' stress scenario to the model; acceptance: each enterprise's margin is reported under both.

claim: 113 of 316 resolved questions carry only agent-recommended answers 'pending owner ratification', and 211 are business-policy decisions; no clause claims legal, CPA, bank or auditor approval. The baseline is labelled authoritative while a third of its resolutions are unratified AI recommendations.
why_it_matters: A sponsor's counsel and auditor cannot rely on positions that the product owner has not ratified; misrepresenting them as authoritative is a governance and sales-diligence risk.
recommended_change: Add an acceptance criterion to CNV-GOV-007: any clause whose resolving question is agent-recommended SHALL display 'unratified' in the baseline index and SHALL NOT be cited in customer-facing material until ratified; acceptance: index shows ratification status per clause.

claim: Minimum mandatory human work per sponsor is underestimated for small sponsors: the 2.5 FTE decision floor binds below ~10,700 funds, yet the CF lower bound assumes existing staff whose time is 'free' except for time used; real CF staff also carry non-DAF programmes, and the double-absence December coverage, three-person rule before auditor acceptance, monthly controller sign-off and quarterly board reporting add fixed time that the model's per-item workload ignores.
why_it_matters: Fixed governance and control-operation time, not exception volume, dominates cost for the sponsors Unbound proposes to target.
recommended_change: Add a fixed-control-time parameter per sponsor (board, controller, compliance, SoD, roster coverage hours/yr) derived from a role-by-role control inventory; acceptance: model reports fixed control hours per sponsor separately from item-driven workload.

claim: December exception SLA attainment falls to 0.70-0.73 for E1, E3, E4 and E5 at modelled staffing, and base economics already assume ~20% of items miss SLA. Donors' highest-value moment (year-end giving and completed-gift timing) is where service degrades; the surge requirement (TEV-001) adds pre-contracted reviewers whose cost is not in the C totals ('no change in cost because surge is absorbed by backlog').
why_it_matters: Donors switching for better service will see worse December performance than incumbents with seasonal staff; the C cost understates the cost of meeting the TEV-001 gate.
recommended_change: Re-run C with the TEV-001 surge plan costed (pre-appointed reviewers, retainer and premium) and require that published C costs meet the sponsor's approved December SLA floor; acceptance: december_peak scenario at >= approved floor with its incremental cost reported.

claim: Donors have weak reasons to switch: they cannot move a fund, only recommend a grant to a new sponsor subject to the old sponsor's approval; history portability is poor (AEF's new portal showed only two years). The donor value proposition in report 05 is lower fees, but the licence is ~4% of E1 sponsor revenue, so any fee cut is a sponsor pricing choice, not something Unbound delivers.
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/05-ECONOMIC-VALIDATION.md:53 (EV-08: price is the main competitive lever)
why_it_matters: Donor-led demand will not pull sponsors onto Unbound; adoption must be sold to sponsor boards on cost and risk, which reinforces the B-vs-C and activation-gate findings.
recommended_change: Add a requirement that donor-side history import from the predecessor platform covers the full fund life (contributions, grants, acknowledgments) with a reconciliation report, so sponsor switching does not degrade donor records; acceptance: migration test imports >= 7 years of history with zero unreconciled items.

claim: Release 1 relies on verified ACH by default and networked rail partners. Charities already enrol separately with Fidelity EFT, PayPal Grant Payments, Chariot Disbursements and others; another enrolment with a new sponsor's rail adds friction, and no sponsor today requires EFT. Check-share reductions (check_share_mult 0.2 in C) assume charities comply.
evidence: /home/user/daf-landscape/research/DAF-INDUSTRY-REPORT-2026-11.md:494-498 (no sponsor requires EFT; NPT/Vanguard use PayPal Grant Payments)
why_it_matters: Charities will not adopt a new enrolment for small grant volumes from a new sponsor; check share stays high and the payment lever shrinks.
recommended_change: Add a requirement to accept existing charity payment enrolments through named networked rail partners (no new charity enrolment for networked charities) and an evidence task measuring the share of target-sponsor grantees reachable that way.

claim: Integration dependencies are on the critical path but have no cost or schedule: per-sponsor ODFI TPSP agreements, rail-partner agreements (some rail operators are competitors, e.g. Chariot within TIFIN), custodian feeds that must be verified per custodian, sponsor ERP integrations, and the California Registry data access whose availability is unknown.
why_it_matters: Each integration is an external dependency that can delay a sponsor's go-live or impose a rail fee, yet the vendor cost model contains no integration engineering or partner fees beyond per-item rail costs.
recommended_change: Add an integration register requirement: each external dependency SHALL have a named counterparty, contract status, cost bearer, lead time and fallback; acceptance: a sponsor activation plan cannot be marked ready while any mandatory dependency lacks an executed agreement.

claim: The intended UI/application stack (Echelon: Limen, Forma, Folio) is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, versions disagree between tags, registry and Unbound's vendored copies, and Limen lacks IdP/session/tenant capability and cannot host embeddable widgets. Commercial licensing is recorded as a launch blocker.
why_it_matters: A single-maintainer, noncommercially licensed dependency is a concentration and IP risk for a commercial vendor and for sponsors' vendor diligence.
recommended_change: Add an architecture decision: no release-1 dependency without an executed commercial licence and escrow or a fork right; acceptance: SBOM licence check fails on PolyForm Noncommercial components.

claim: Concentration risk is structural: (1) addressable sponsors of meaningful size are few (39 non-processor sponsors with 1,000-60,000 accounts hold ~242k accounts, many captive to wealth firms on Ren); (2) early Unbound revenue will depend on 1-5 sponsors; (3) sponsor exits (CNV-ENT-002) are designed to be cheap, which lowers switching costs for Unbound's own customers as much as for incumbents'.
evidence: /home/user/daf-landscape/data/mission-2026-11-14/dafrc-sponsor-schedule-d-fy2019-2024.csv FY2024 recomputation (1,000-60,000 accounts, average balance >= $20k: 39 sponsors, 241,812 accounts, $157.5bn)
why_it_matters: Loss of one anchor sponsor in years 1-3 would remove a large share of revenue; Ren's own CF attrition (5 of 28) shows sponsors do move.
recommended_change: Add a business policy limiting reliance on any single sponsor (e.g. no sponsor > 25% of ARR after year 3) and a model scenario for loss of the largest sponsor; evidence task: name the target sponsor list and incumbents for each.

claim: Sponsor configuration is still heavy despite simplification: 13 outcome questions plus 14 explicit values, versioned policy packs requiring affirmative adoption with independent approval for material changes, shadow replay before rollout, and mapping of each activation element to decisions and evidence. Small sponsors lack the staff to evaluate policy-pack changes, and the cost of each regulatory change is $100/fund for E2.
why_it_matters: Configuration governance falls on exactly the small sponsors least able to perform it; unadopted changes accumulate drift risk.
recommended_change: Add an acceptance criterion: a sponsor with no adopted response to a mandatory policy-pack change within its deadline SHALL have the affected feature fail safe, and onboarding usability SHALL be validated with at least five small-sponsor staff completing configuration unaided in under a set time.

claim: Workplace giving (E4) is shown as 'thin' at +$5/fund, but that already uses the $28 licence at 1M platform funds; at the adverse $49 licence E4 C costs $79-90 against $60 revenue, and at 100k platform funds $121. E4 is not viable on any realistic platform scale, and the model itself shows a self-built AI-enhanced operation is cheaper at 2M funds.
evidence: scratchpad work/exp*.py (re-runs of enterprise_economics.py with overrides; repository unchanged) exp.py licence-scale rows
why_it_matters: Keeping E4 as a modelled enterprise invites architectural and sales effort on a segment the economics reject.
recommended_change: Record E4 as an accepted limitation (not a release-1 segment) with an explicit reopening trigger: executed employer funding of >= C cost at adverse licence.

claim: Automation rates are not literal rates in the model: 'human interventions per 1,000 funds' fall from 2,718 (A) to 563 (C) for E1. Of C's assumed improvement, AI inference is <=$1/fund, so the 'AI-native' label is not what produces the result; the savings are workflow policy (delegation, reuse, outsourcing) that require board and auditor acceptance, not technology.
why_it_matters: Marketing the product as AI-native overstates the technology moat and understates the governance change customers must make.
recommended_change: Business policy: customer-facing economic claims SHALL attribute savings by lever (policy delegation, determination reuse, outsourcing, software) with each lever's activation gate listed.

claim: Comparator AL (traditional workflow on licensed software) uses Unbound's own $28 licence as the incumbent software price; incumbent pricing (Foundant, Ren, NPact/FIMS, Blackbaud) is not public and not researched, so the 'build vs buy' and 'redesign adds a third' conclusions for CFs are untested against actual competitor prices.
evidence: /home/user/unbound/requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/model/enterprise_economics.py:88-94 (AL: 'technology bought at the same licence as C')
why_it_matters: If incumbents price below or near Unbound for small tenants, the residual C advantage for CFs (already negative at median sizes) disappears entirely.
recommended_change: Evidence task: obtain at least three incumbent quotes or contract values (via 990 Part VII-B contractor payments, RFPs, or sponsor interviews) for CF and mid-size sponsors; re-run AL with those prices.

claim: Revenue resilience to markets is overstated for Unbound: report 05 notes a 30% decline cuts E1 sponsor margin from $582 to $426, but Unbound's per-fund licence is decoupled from AUM, so Unbound bears none of that shock, while sponsor customers under margin pressure will renegotiate the licence; the market-downturn stress also shows uncontained exposure of $5.1M (E1) to $25.6M (E5) that is not priced.
why_it_matters: Downturns hit customer budgets and renewal pricing; the exposure figures suggest liability and insurance cost not reflected in either party's cost.
recommended_change: Add a renewal-price-pressure scenario (licence -20% in downturn years) to the vendor P&L and require the uncontained-exposure figure to map to a named bearer and insurance cover.

claim: No requirement gates commercial commitments on the evidence backlog. CNV-EVB-001 only requires unmeasured values to be labelled 'scenario assumption'; pricing (CNV-ECO-002) is gated only by sponsor CFO approval of fee schedules. Unbound could sign licence prices before exception incidence, minutes, complex hours, reuse share or December arrivals are measured.
why_it_matters: The whole business case's failure conditions are listed but nothing prevents committing to prices or segments before they are tested.
recommended_change: Add an acceptance criterion: no licence price list, customer cost-saving claim or segment commitment SHALL be approved until a shadow replay of at least 12 months of a real sponsor's grant history and a 90-day time study have measured exception incidence, minutes, reuse share and complex-gift hours, and the C case remains below B at P50 using measured values.
